title: Celebrate tiny progress
description: Progress is usually too small to see day by day. Noticing it on purpose keeps motivation alive between big milestones.

body.heading: Small wins are real wins
paragraphs: Finished the boring email. Practised for ten minutes. Cooked instead of ordering in. These moments feel too minor to mention, yet they are exactly what a good week is made of.
When you only count large achievements, most days register as failures, which is both untrue and discouraging. A fairer scoreboard changes how the whole project feels.

body.heading: Keep the evidence where you can see it
paragraphs: Try a simple ritual: at the end of the day, write down one thing that moved forward, however slightly. Some people keep a jar of folded notes, a line in a journal, or a photo album of works in progress.
On a discouraging day, read a few entries back. You are not inflating your achievements; you are correcting the bias that makes slow progress invisible.

takeaway: Write down one small forward step each day, and let the list argue with your doubts.
